title: Harold Malmgren's CIA connections and IDA cover

tellings.quote: Okay, here are a few a few fun facts. If you watch that interview I did with him, he says I was best friends with Tom Farmer. Happened to be the GC, the general counsel of the CIA.
He had Paul Melon's walking stick in the interview, and I'm holding it for half the time in the interview
tellings.difference: Adds that Michels held Paul Mellon's walking stick during the interview, and mentions Dean Johnson and Malmgren's diary.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Michels telling of Malmgren's hidden CIA connections (Tom Farmer, Paul Mellon) as they came out in his interview.

as_told.title: Malmgren's hidden CIA ties and Paul Mellon's walking stick

plain: Michels argues that Harold Malmgren, a veteran Washington economic official he interviewed, had deep ties to the CIA from the 1960s on, with work at IDA, a defense research body, serving as a cover. As Michels tells it from his own interview, Malmgren said he was best friends with Tom Farmer, the CIA's general counsel, or chief lawyer, and he names others in that circle, such as Richard Bissell and Paul Mellon. Michels adds that he held Paul Mellon's walking stick for half the interview and mentions Malmgren's diary.
